sections.title: The group ght
paragraphs: The letters ght end with the sound in (night) /naɪt/, the dark time of day. In this spelling, the letters gh make no sound at all. Only the final letter t is spoken. This group has only one sound pattern in words like this.

sections.title: Pronouncing the group
paragraphs: Do not make any sound in your throat for the letters gh. Move straight from the vowel to the final letter t. Touch the ridge behind your upper teeth with your tongue tip. Stop the air for a moment, then release it with a small burst. The sound is voiceless, so your throat does not shake. You can feel a small puff of air on your fingers.

sections.title: When to keep silent
paragraphs: When the letters gh appear right before the letter t, they are silent. A silent letter is a letter that you write but do not say. You hear this in the word (light) /laɪt/. You jump directly to the final consonant sound, as heard in (sight) /saɪt/.

sections.title: Common speaking errors
paragraphs: Do not make a rough scraping sound in your throat for the letters gh. Many learners try to pronounce these letters like a friction sound in their own language. Keep your throat quiet and say only the final letter t.
